references.text: Psalm 24:8 also describes the Lord as 'strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle,' which directly corresponds to the description of the Lord as a warrior.
Isaiah 42:13 uses the same image and says that 'the Lord goes out like a mighty man, like a warrior he stirs up his zeal,' repeating the theme from Exodus 15:3.
Zephaniah 3:17 speaks of the Lord who is 'mighty to save,' showing God's power to fight for His people.
In Exodus 14:14, Moses says that 'the Lord will fight for you,' which is the immediate context for the song of praise in chapter 15.
Moses reminds the people that 'the Lord your God, He will fight for you,' confirming God's role as a warrior for Israel.
Exodus 3:15 establishes that 'the Lord' (YHWH) is God's name forever, which corresponds to 'the Lord is His name' in 15:3.
Revelation 19:11-16 depicts Christ as the heavenly warrior who comes to fight against God's enemies, an eschatological fulfillment of the image from Exodus 15:3.
Amos 5:8 also uses the expression 'the Lord is His name' to emphasize God's identity and power.
Direct allusion to the exodus; Isaiah confirms God's identity as a fighting Savior over the sea.
